reason: The frame sections and cargo mesh seem suited to making tracks that spread the rover's weight across the drift.
expectation: I expect them to form some kind of support track, though I don't know exactly what it will look like.

alternatives.reason: Sieving gravel might help prepare the crossing, but the frame and mesh seem more directly suited to supporting the wheels.

effect: The panels spread wheel loads and can hold gravel, so preparing gravel looks like the next step.
reaction: The raised edges give the panels a useful purpose beyond supporting the wheels.
reason: Sieving the firm gravel patch is the only numbered action offered and may provide material for the panels.
expectation: I expect to obtain graded gravel suitable for the traction panels, though the result could be different.

effect: The sieve produced coarse gravel, which appears ready to fill the traction panels.
reaction: The result is straightforward and fits the crossing plan.
reason: Combining the gravel with the panels is the only numbered action offered and should prepare them for the soft crossing.
expectation: I expect gravel-filled traction panels that can support the rover's wheels on the drift.

effect: The completed tracks combine the panels and gravel into a surface that supports the wheels and keeps the stones from spreading into the drift.
reaction: The explanation of how the frames contain the gravel made the finished tracks satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the traction panels was most worthwhile: their mesh bottoms spread the wheel load, while raised edges hold the gravel.

leastWorthwhile.text: Sieving the gravel was straightforward and had little explanation on its own.

surprise.text: I had expected the panels to support the wheels, but their role in keeping gravel from spreading sideways added to my understanding.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each contributed clearly to preparing the crossing.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to see what happens when the expedition follows the seam and tries to recover an intact sample; the crossing preparation leaves that prospect open.
